unit.title: Replace a leaking cache with a bounded LRU

fund-java/16-jvm-memory-and-gc/01-bounde.instructions:
**Skills:** LinkedHashMap access order · bounded caches  
**Level:** ★★☆

**Interview prompt.** "Our exchange-rate service caches lookups in a static HashMap keyed by (currency, date). After two weeks in production the heap is full. Bound it."

**Why it matters.** An unbounded cache is a memory leak with good intentions. A LinkedHashMap in access order with `removeEldestEntry` is a correct size-bounded LRU in a few lines.

**Your task.** Implement `static <K, V> Map<K, V> lruCache(int maxEntries)`:
- the returned map never holds more than `maxEntries` entries
- when a put would exceed the limit, the LEAST RECENTLY USED entry is evicted
- `get` and `put` both count as uses (a read moves the entry to most-recent); `containsKey` does not
- iteration order is least recently used first
- `maxEntries` below 1 throws `IllegalArgumentException`

**Worked example.** Max 2: put a, put b, get a, put c: b is evicted and the keys are `[a, c]`.
hints: LinkedHashMap can keep its entries in access order and has a hook that runs after every insertion.
Configure the map to order its entries by access instead of insertion, and override its eviction hook so it drops the eldest entry once the size passes the limit; validate the limit first.
Use a map that remembers which entries were touched most recently, and tell it to drop its oldest entry whenever adding one pushes it past the limit.
